title: Beyond the 956: Michael Hampton, Parliament-Funkadelic guitarist known as 'Kidd Funkadelic,' dies at 70
excerpt: Michael Hampton, the guitarist known as “Kidd Funkadelic” who powered Parliament-Funkadelic for five decades, died on November 23, 2026. He was 70.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Michael Hampton, a lead guitarist for Parliament-Funkadelic known as “Kidd Funkadelic,” has died at 70.

Hampton’s death was announced on November 23, 2026, by Zebulon, the Los Angeles venue where he had played a show of his own on November 18. No cause of death has been reported. He had turned 70 just a week earlier.

A Cleveland native, Hampton joined the band at 17, stepping into the spot left by Eddie Hazel, the guitarist behind the 10-minute instrumental “Maggot Brain.” Hampton took the nickname Kidd Funkadelic and kept playing that song at P-Funk shows for the next five decades.

Hampton made his Funkadelic recording debut on the 1975 album Let’s Take It to the Stage. He played on records from both Parliament and Funkadelic, as well as albums by spinoff acts such as Bootsy’s Rubber Band and the Brides of Funkenstein. After George Clinton disbanded the P-Funk organization in 1981, Hampton kept working, playing on Clinton’s solo records and on albums by Sly & Robbie, Digital Underground and Too $hort. He is credited as a co-writer on Digital Underground’s “Wussup Wit the Luv.”

In 1997, Hampton was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Parliament-Funkadelic. He released his first solo album, Heavy Metal Funkason, in 1998, and he was still touring with Parliament-Funkadelic this year.

Sources: Stereogum; 105.1 The Bounce; Zebulon announcement.
